practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should focus on a single behavior with one Arrange-Act-Assert. RATIONALE: Single-focus aids diagnosis and maintainability. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant requires one method call and one assertion group; non-compliant if multiple Acts or multiple scenarios. DECISION RULES: The method has a single Act (new Grafo()) but no explicit Arrange-Act-Assert block or assertions; rule 3 (one Act + one assertion group) is not satisfied. VERDICT: non-compliant because there is no assertion or clear Assert phase.

PRINCIPLE: Tests must not depend on each other; use setup/teardown when shared state exists. RATIONALE: Independence allows arbitrary execution order and parallel runs. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if tests use local variables only or proper @Before/@After. DECISION RULES: The method uses only local variables and does not modify shared/static state; no ordered naming. VERDICT: compliant — the single test is self-contained and does not rely on shared state.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should include happy path and error scenarios. RATIONALE: Ensures robustness and correct exception handling. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant requires at least two tests (happy + error) for a method or explicit exception tests. DECISION RULES: The class has only one test method and it exercises only a constructor happy path with no exception or invalid-input tests. VERDICT: non-compliant — no coverage of exceptional/error flows is present.

PRINCIPLE: Test boundaries at min/max and just outside. RATIONALE: Boundaries are common error sources. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant when tests include empty, zero, negative, max values. DECISION RULES: The tested code is a no-argument constructor with no obvious numeric/string inputs; therefore boundary analysis is not applicable. VERDICT: not-applicable because there are no input boundaries to exercise in this test.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should be self-contained and reusable; extract helpers for duplication. RATIONALE: Reduces duplication and improves maintainability. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if helper methods/constants are used or tests are short and non-duplicative. DECISION RULES: The test is very short (<10 lines) with no duplicated blocks in this class context. VERDICT: compliant — no repetition and small footprint.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Keep tests small, avoid loops/complex conditionals. RATIONALE: Simpler tests are less error-prone. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if methods <20 lines and no loops/complex conditionals. DECISION RULES: The method is short and linear with no loops or conditionals. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Assertions should be comprehensive and verify multiple properties. RATIONALE: Deep checks detect subtle faults. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant when multiple properties or meaningful assertions are present. DECISION RULES: The test has zero assertions (not even assertNotNull); rule 1 indicates that having only superficial or zero assertions is non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant due to lack of assertions verifying properties of the created object.

PRINCIPLE: Avoid ignored or commented-out tests; keep suite active. RATIONALE: Ignored tests hide issues. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if no @Ignore/@Disabled nor commented-out @Test. DECISION RULES: No @Ignore/@Disabled annotations or commented-out tests are present. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should link to requirements/tickets. RATIONALE: Traceability aids impact analysis. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if annotations or Javadoc reference requirement IDs. DECISION RULES: No @Story/@Requirement annotations or Javadoc references to REQ-/JIRA- IDs are present. VERDICT: non-compliant — no traceability metadata.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Performance/security tests are separate from unit tests. RATIONALE: Non-functional tests require dedicated approaches. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Typically not applicable for unit tests unless explicit timing/security checks are present. DECISION RULES: No timing or security assertions and class name doesn't indicate a performance test. VERDICT: not-applicable.

PRINCIPLE: Test names should describe scenario and expected result. RATIONALE: Descriptive names help diagnose failures. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant when names follow methodName_scenario_expectedResult or BDD style. DECISION RULES: The method name 'test0' is generic and conveys no scenario or expectation. VERDICT: non-compliant due to poor naming.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Generated tests should be minimal and intention-revealing. RATIONALE: Heavy generated code is verbose and hard to maintain. EVALUATION CRITERIA: non-compliant if auto-generated comments or generated names like test0 are present. DECISION RULES: File header explicitly states 'automatically generated by EvoSuite' and the method is named 'test0', matching auto-generated patterns. VERDICT: non-compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should be thoughtfully designed (TDD/BDD) with Given-When-Then structure. RATIONALE: Test-first design increases coverage and clarity. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if Given-When-Then comments or BDD-style naming are present or multiple scenarios covered. DECISION RULES: The single minimal/generated test lacks BDD structure and covers only a trivial happy path. VERDICT: non-compliant — no evident prioritized design.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should focus on public behavior not internal implementation. RATIONALE: Behavior-focused tests are less brittle. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if tests only call public APIs and avoid reflection/internal fields. DECISION RULES: The test only invokes the public constructor and does not access private fields or use reflection. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Use clear, specific assertions with messages. RATIONALE: Specific assertions make failures diagnosable. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant when specific assertions or messages are used; non-compliant when assertions are generic or absent. DECISION RULES: This test has zero assertions, violating the expectation to assert behavior. VERDICT: non-compliant due to missing assertions.

PRINCIPLE: Comments should explain 'why', not 'what'; avoid commented-out code. RATIONALE: Minimal helpful comments improve clarity. EVALUATION CRITERIA: non-compliant if commented-out code or excessive comments present. DECISION RULES: File contains a short auto-generated header comment but no commented-out test code; comments are not excessive. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests must be deterministic and avoid randomness/time without mocking. RATIONALE: Determinism avoids flaky tests. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if no Random(), current time usage, Thread.sleep(), or external dependencies without mocking. DECISION RULES: The test only constructs a Grafo and does not use random/time or external systems. VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should not modify shared state or require cleanup. RATIONALE: Avoids inter-test coupling and resource leaks. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if tests do not persist data or modify static state. DECISION RULES: This test only uses a local variable and does not create files, DB records, or modify statics. VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Use tags/categories to organize and selectively run tests. RATIONALE: Labels help CI filtering and resource management. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if @Tag/@Category used meaningfully. DECISION RULES: No @Tag/@Category annotations are present at class or method level. VERDICT: non-compliant — no categorization provided.
